PARTNERSHIP ONBOARDING · CUSTOMER SUPPORT
Standard Meds × Logicall
Customer Support Playbook
What existing patients call about, and what you do in each case. Built from the real
Standard Meds support inbox and from every question your team has raised in our
shared Slack channel. Every case has what to do on the call, and anything not
covered goes to Slack.
WHO CALLS APPLIES TO WHERE YOU WORK VERSION
Existing patients All verticals Dosable · ReFlow V1 · living document
How to Use This Page
01
Page 1 of 19

Every situation below is a box: what the patient says, and what you do.
THE TWO RULES THAT APPLY TO EVERY CALL ON THIS PAGE
Cancellations: ask why. For a side effect, their own doctor's advice, a repeat request, or a
purchase they say they didn't make, you cancel right away. For most other reasons you
make one offer (two for price) and, if the patient says no, you cancel on the same call. See
the table in §3.
Refunds: Standard Meds decides each case under our refund policy. Do not promise a
refund, do not refuse one. Post the order ID in our shared Slack channel and we take it from
there. See §8.
EVERYTHING FROM THE RECOVERY PLAYBOOKS STILL APPLIES
Identify yourself, confirm you are speaking with the patient (name and email on the order)
before discussing anything about their account, no medical advice, never quote a price or a
discount that isn't in this hub, never read card details into notes. This page only adds what is
specific to support calls.
ESCALATION PATH
Anything this page doesn't cover, or anything you need to escalate, goes straight into our
shared Slack channel, one thread per case, with the order ID and vertical. Never paste the
patient's full name, phone, email or any health detail in Slack, the order ID is enough for us to
find them.
Why Patients Contact Us
02
From 682 patient emails to support@standardmeds.com, April – September 2026. One email
can raise more than one topic, so the shares don't add to 100%.
TOPIC SHARE OF EMAILS WHERE ON THIS PAGE
Wants to cancel 44.6% §3
Order hasn't arrived / delayed 9.7% §5
Didn't realize it was a subscription 7.5% §3, §4
Page 2 of 19

Can't log in / login link / portal 7.2% §6
Doesn't recognize a charge 7.0% §4
Side effect 6.3% §7
Waiting on a refund 4.5% §8
Order status 4.5% §5
Can't reach anyone 3.5% §9
Surprised by the upgrade (upsell) charge 2.8% §4
ID / document still pending 2.5% §7
Cancelled but was still charged or shipped 2.1% §3
TWO THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE YOUR FIRST SUPPORT CALL
Almost half of all contacts are cancellations. Most support calls will start with "I want to
cancel". §3 is the section to know best.
Many of our patients are older and not comfortable online. Patients tell us they are in
their 80s, use a landline, or can't manage the portal. Expect to walk people through screens
slowly, and sometimes to talk with a spouse or adult child (see §9).
Cancellations
03
Ask why first. The reason decides whether you cancel right away, make one offer, or send the
patient to support@standardmeds.com.
OFFERS HAVE A LIMIT
When a reason allows an offer, you make one (for "I can't afford it", at most two, see the box).
If the patient says no, you cancel on the same call. Don't ask again, don't transfer them, don't
make them call back. Cancelling has to be as easy as signing up. That's the law, not only our
policy.
WHY THEY WANT TO CANCEL WHAT YOU DO
Page 3 of 19

Side effect or allergic reaction Cancel right away. No offer. Box below.
"My own doctor told me not to take it" Cancel right away. No offer. Box below.
Already asked to cancel before Cancel right away. No offer. Box below.
"It didn't work for me" One offer: the provider in the Medical Chat. If no, cancel.
"I can't afford it" Up to two offers: 25% off next month, then 25% off every
month. If no, cancel.
"I have too much product" / "I want a One offer: pause. If no, cancel.
break"
"I didn't make this purchase" / "I forgot I Cancel right away. No offer. Box below.
signed up"
Side effect or allergic reaction
PATIENT: "I had a reaction to it, I want to stop." · "I'm allergic." · "It made me sick."
WHAT YOU DO
1. If they describe a severe reaction happening now (trouble breathing, swelling of the face,
lips or throat), tell them to call 911 before anything else.
2. Cancel the subscription in Dosable. You are authorized to do it on this call.
3. Tell the patient the subscription is cancelled and no further refills will be sent or charged.
4. Ask the patient to report the side effect to their provider in the Medical Chat (Medical Chat
playbook), so the provider knows.
5. Log what the patient told you, in their words, in the notes. No diagnosis, no opinion.
Don't comment on the symptom and don't suggest what caused it. That's for the provider.
"My own doctor told me not to take it"
PATIENT: "My doctor said I shouldn't take this." · "My doctor wants me off it."
WHAT YOU DO
1. Don't argue with the patient's doctor and don't make an offer.
2. Cancel the subscription in Dosable on this call.
3. Tell the patient it's cancelled and no further refills will be sent or charged.
If they also ask for their money back, follow §8.
Page 4 of 19

Asked to cancel before, still being contacted, charged or shipped
PATIENT: "This is my second request." · "I already cancelled, why are you still calling me?" · "I
cancelled and got charged anyway."
This is where disputes and chargebacks come from. Patients in this situation have gone to their
bank or a lawyer.
WHAT YOU DO
1. Apologize, don't argue, don't defend the charge, don't make an offer.
2. Check the subscription in Dosable first. Sometimes the patient thinks they cancelled, but the
cancellation never went through.
3. If it's still active: tell the patient clearly that it wasn't cancelled and is still active, then cancel it
now, on this call.
"I checked, and your subscription was never cancelled, it's still active. I'm cancelling it for
you right now."
4. If it was cancelled and they were still charged: post the order ID in our shared Slack channel,
marked urgent: cancelled and still charged, explaining that the patient cancelled and was
charged afterwards. Standard Meds reviews it for a refund. Don't promise the refund on the
call. Tell the patient our team is reviewing it.
5. Don't call this patient again about anything else.
"It didn't work for me"
PATIENT: "I don't feel any difference." · "It's not doing anything."
YOUR ONE OFFER
Suggest the patient tell their provider in the Medical Chat before stopping. The provider is the one
who can review it. You never comment on the treatment or suggest a dose yourself.
"Before you stop, would you like to let your provider know in the Medical Chat? They can
review how it's going with you."
If the patient says no, cancel in Dosable on this call.
"I can't afford it"
PATIENT: "It's too expensive." · "I can't pay this every month."
UP TO TWO OFFERS, IN THIS ORDER
The most you can give is 25%. For a patient on $99 a month, that's about $75 a month. Never
go below that.
Page 5 of 19

"NEXT ORDER
OFFER WHAT THE PATIENT GETS
ONLY"
1st 25% off the next renewal only Ticked
2nd, only if they said no to 25% off every renewal, for as long as Unticked
the 1st they stay
1st: "I can offer you 25% off your next month."
2nd: "I checked with my team, and we'd like to offer you 25% off every month for as long as
you're with us."
If they say no to the second offer, cancel. No third offer.
HOW TO APPLY IT IN DOSABLE
1. Open the patient's order in Dosable. Under Quick Actions, click Order Details.
The order page. Order Details is the first button under Quick Actions.
2. There's no 25% button. Type the discounted price in the Original Price field: the normal price ×
0.75. For example, $99 → $74.25, $297 → $222.75.
3. 1st offer: tick "Next order only", so the price goes back to normal after the next renewal. 2nd
offer: leave it unticked, so the discount stays on the subscription.
4. Click Update Order.
Page 6 of 19

Type the price in Original Price. Next order only at the bottom: ticked for the 1st offer, unticked
for the 2nd. Don't use the preset buttons, they stop at 20%.
5. Tell the patient the new price and how long it lasts: next renewal only (1st offer) or every
renewal while they stay (2nd offer). Never leave it vague.
If the patient says no, cancel in Dosable on this call.
"I didn't make this purchase" / "I forgot I signed up"
PATIENT: "I never ordered this." · "I forgot I signed up." · "I didn't know I'd be charged."
WHAT YOU DO
1. If the patient doesn't recognize the charge, first check §4. Many turn out to be the upgrade
offer.
2. If they still want to cancel, cancel in Dosable on this call. No offer.
3. Tell the patient it's cancelled and no further refills will be sent or charged. If they ask for their
money back, follow §8.
Pause instead of cancel
PATIENT: "I want to stop for now." · "I have enough for a while."
WHAT YOU DO
1. Pause the subscription yourself, on the call: open the order in Dosable and click Pause under
Quick Actions. The pause is for one month.
2. Tell the patient how it works:
"I've paused your subscription for one month. After that, it renews automatically. If you'd
like to extend the pause, you can manage your subscription in the patient portal."
Page 7 of 19

Pausing is better than cancelling if they might change their mind: resuming is easier than starting
over. If they'd rather cancel, cancel on the call.
Bought the upgrade by mistake, wants to keep only the original plan
PATIENT: "I only wanted the 1-month plan, but I also got charged for 12 months." · "There's a $1,188
charge on my card."
WHAT WE KNOW
After checkout, the patient sees an upgrade offer. Accepting it creates a second order
alongside the first.
In Dosable you can't remove just the upgrade. Don't cancel anything yourself. Ruben guides
how to proceed.
Before the patient is prescribed, the amount is an authorization hold, not a final charge. The
card is only charged once the provider prescribes.
WHAT YOU DO
1. Don't cancel anything in Dosable.
2. Post in the Dosable Slack channel, tagging Ruben: the order ID, and that the patient wants to
cancel one of the orders (the upgrade) and keep the other. Order ID only, no name, email or
phone.
3. In the same message, ask him directly for a new checkout link without the upgrade:
"@Ruben order [ID]: the patient wants to cancel the upsell order and keep the original one.
Can you send a new checkout link with only the original plan, without the upsell?"
4. Follow Ruben's instructions on how to proceed.
5. Tell the patient the hold from the cancelled order disappears from their statement within 7
days. If it's still there after 7 days, they should email support@standardmeds.com.
Charges & Billing
04
"What is this charge?" calls, card updates and failed payments.
"I don't recognize this charge"
PATIENT: "Is it you who charged me?" · "There's a charge I don't know."
WHAT YOU TELL THEM
Page 8 of 19

Our charges appear on bank statements as . NTRO Health is the
STNDMEDS* NTROHEALTH
company behind Standard Meds.
ChemistryRx and EpiqScripts are our partner pharmacies. Their names can appear on the
order, on the medication label and in the patient portal, but not on the bank statement. If a
patient says they saw a different name on their statement, ask for a screenshot or exactly
where they saw it and post it in Slack.
The payment receipt doesn't name the product. If the patient asks what they bought, look up
the order in Dosable and tell them the product and plan.
Two orders for the same patient usually means they accepted the upgrade offer after
checkout. It's not a duplicate. The first order is the first month they bought; the second is the
upgrade, covering the rest of the months they accepted. That's why there are two charges.
If, after that, the patient says they did not make the purchase, cancel right away. See §3.
"I didn't know this was a subscription"
PATIENT: "I thought it was a one-time purchase." · "Why was I charged again?"
WHAT YOU TELL THEM
All our plans are subscriptions, including the 1-month plan.
If they want to stop, offer the pause (§3). If they want to cancel, follow §3.
Update the card on file
PATIENT: "I want to change my card before the next charge."
TWO WAYS, BOTH IN DOSABLE
1. From the order: open the patient's order → payment method box → Update Card → enter card
number, expiration, CVV and the card's billing address → save.
2. Through Masquerade: click the patient's name and email at the top right → My Billing
Information → Edit Payment Information. The same pop-up opens.
KNOWN ISSUE: THE UPDATE CARD BUTTON DOESN'T APPEAR
Some agents intermittently don't get the button. Try an incognito / private window. If it
still doesn't show, have another agent try. If nobody can, post the order ID in Slack. It's a
Dosable issue we're tracking with them.
The full card-update walkthrough, with screenshots, is in the Renewals playbook.
Renewal failed ("Rebill Failed")
PATIENT: "Why didn't my refill come?"
Page 9 of 19

ReFlow shows you the decline reason. It's for us only. Never tell the patient the reason
("insufficient funds" etc.). Keep it neutral:
"Your renewal payment didn't go through. To keep your treatment going we just need to
update the card on file."
If the patient wants to keep the same card (for example, they blocked the charge because they
didn't recognize it), leave the payment method as it is. The system retries automatically after
some time. You don't need to force the rebill.
Card keeps getting declined at checkout
PATIENT: "I tried several times and it keeps saying declined." · "I only have this one card."
After several attempts, the card gets flagged as possible fraud, and every new attempt makes
it worse. Stop retrying.
The patient should call their bank and say they're trying to make this purchase. Once the bank
clears it, they try again.
HSA / FSA cards
PATIENT: "Can I pay with my HSA card?"
Yes. Patients can pay directly with an HSA or FSA card. About 1 in 10 of our patients do.
Price questions from existing patients
PATIENT: "Will my price go up?" · "Can I get a discount?"
"WILL MY PRICE GO UP?"
Yes, after the first month. Be clear about it:
PRODUCT FIRST MONTH FROM THE 2ND MONTH
NeuroCalmRx $99 $149
TriShotRx (ED) $99 $149
LiftRx (facial anti-aging) $49 $149
"CAN I GET A DISCOUNT?"
Don't answer that there are no discounts. That's often when the patient decides to cancel.
Go up step by step, only when the patient says no to the previous step:
Page 10 of 19

1. 10% off. It's often enough.
2. 20% off.
3. 25% off. That's the highest percentage you can give.
4. If they still want to cancel: offer to keep them at $99 a month (also for LiftRx). This is the
last offer.
10% and 20% are preset buttons in Order Details. For 25% or $99, type the price in the
Original Price field. See the "I can't afford it" box in §3 for where to find them.
If they say no to the last offer, cancel on the call.
Coupon is for new orders only: 10% off the first month on every product.
CALL10
Orders & Delivery
05
Where's my order, why is it late, and the tracking number that "doesn't work".
"Where is my order?" / "It's late"
PATIENT: "It's been a week." · "I was told 2 days." · "When will it arrive?"
WHY IT TAKES A FEW DAYS
All our products are compounded medications, made for each patient. We don't keep any stock:
the pharmacy makes the medication fresh for that patient, so they receive a truly fresh
medication.
"Your medication is compounded specifically for you, so it isn't sitting on a shelf. Our partner
pharmacy prepares it fresh after your provider prescribes it. That usually takes 2 to 3 days,
and shipping takes up to about 4 more days."
Production: 2 to 3 days after the prescription. It can take longer when the partner pharmacies
have many orders to prepare.
Shipping: up to about 4 days.
In total: about 7 days from the prescription.
CHECK WHERE THE ORDER IS, STEP BY STEP
1. Not prescribed yet: the patient is almost always waiting on something from their side, the ID or
an answer in the Medical Chat. Follow the Medical Chat playbook.
2. Prescribed, not shipped yet: it's being prepared at the pharmacy. Explain the fresh
compounding above.
3. Shipped: give them the tracking number. On the carrier's website they can see the estimated
delivery date (see the next box if the number "doesn't work").
Page 11 of 19

Don't promise a specific date. Say they'll receive it in the next few days, or point them to the
estimated date on the carrier's website.
FOR REFERENCE: WHAT WE MEASURED ON 1,410 REAL ORDERS
PRODUCT TYPICAL: CHECKOUT → DELIVERED SLOWEST 1 IN 10
TriShotRx about 5 days 9 days
NeuroCalmRx about 7 days 10 days
ZoliraRx about 7 days 10 days
LiftRx about 8 days 11 days
IF THE PATIENT COMPLAINS IT'S LATE
Post it in the late orders thread in our shared Slack channel, with the order ID and what you
see (prescribed or not, shipped or not, tracking status).
If the order has no tracking number, or the tracking can't be followed, say so in the post. A
Standard Meds team member takes care of it with the pharmacy.
"The tracking number doesn't work"
PATIENT: "UPS says the number is invalid." · "I think this is a scam."
A tracking number that starts with 9400 is a USPS number, even if the email says UPS. Have
the patient check it on usps.com.
Reassure them. The carrier label in the email is wrong, not the shipment.
"Can it ship before I send my ID?"
PATIENT: "Can you just send it?"
No. Providers verify identity through a health information exchange. When what the patient
typed doesn't match, they ask for an ID, and nothing is prescribed or shipped until it's sent.
The provider reviews the answers within 24 hours of receiving them.
How to get the ID sent: Medical Chat playbook. Patients who are uneasy about sending it in the
chat can email it to support@standardmeds.com from the email on their order.
Patient just paid but isn't in Dosable yet
PATIENT: "I see the charge on my card, but you can't find me?"
Page 12 of 19

A new order can take up to about an hour to show up in Dosable after checkout. Tell the patient
their order went through and call back later rather than placing a second order.
Wrong dose, wrong quantity or wrong plan
PATIENT: "I ordered 6 doses and got charged for 12." · "This isn't what I ordered."
Same path as the upgrade bought by mistake (§3): you don't change or cancel the order
yourself. Dosable makes the change.
WHAT YOU DO
1. Check the order in Dosable: what the patient bought, and what they say it should be.
2. Post in the Dosable Slack channel, tagging Ruben, with the order ID, what was bought and
what's correct. Order ID only, no name, email or phone.
"@Ruben order [ID]: the patient bought 12 doses, but the correct would be only 6. If
possible, we'd like to change it and update the order."
3. Follow Ruben's instructions, and tell the patient we're correcting it with our team.
Package arrived damaged or leaking
PATIENT: "The medication was leaking through the box." · "It arrived broken."
WHAT YOU DO
1. Ask the patient to email photos of the package and the product to
support@standardmeds.com, from the email on their order.
2. Tell them that once the photos arrive, Standard Meds processes the refund.
3. Post the order ID in Slack so we know to expect the photos.
Package not received, lost or wrong address
PATIENT: "Tracking says delivered but I don't have it." · "It never came." · "I moved."
1. CHECK WHAT HAPPENED TO THE PACKAGE
1. Open the order in Dosable and copy the tracking number.
2. Look it up on the carrier's website (usps.com or fedex.com) and check whether it was
returned to sender.
2A. RETURNED TO SENDER: FIX THE ADDRESS
It usually means the address was invalid or incomplete (missing the apartment, unit, or part of the
street).
1. Ask the patient for their full address.
Page 13 of 19

2. On the order in Dosable, click the Shipping Address box.
The Shipping Address box at the top of the order. Click it to edit.
3. Correct the address. When typing Address 1, pick one of the suggestions so city, state and ZIP
fill in correctly. Use Address Line 2 for apartment or unit. Click Save.
The Edit Shipping Address window. Patient data is blurred in this example.
4. Post the order ID in our shared Slack channel (Logicall × Standard Meds), saying the
address was updated. A Standard Meds team member asks the pharmacy to update the
Page 14 of 19

address and reship.
2B. ANY OTHER CASE (SAYS DELIVERED, STUCK, LOST)
Post the order ID and what the tracking shows in our shared Slack channel. We contact the
pharmacy to find out what happened. Tell the patient our team is checking with the pharmacy.
Portal & Login
06
The patient portal is where patients answer the provider, send their ID and manage billing. Many
of our patients struggle with it.
"I never got the login email"
PATIENT: "I checked spam, there's nothing." · "The link never came."
WORKAROUND
1. In Dosable, open the patient and click Masquerade.
2. Click the name/email at the top right → My Account.
3. Turn on Email Notifications.
Every time this happens, note the order ID and post it in Slack. We're collecting examples for
Dosable to fix the root cause.
"Is there an app?"
No. The portal works in the web browser only, on phone or computer.
Guiding a patient through the portal
PATIENT: "I don't know where to click." · "I'm not good with computers."
Use Masquerade in Dosable to see exactly what the patient sees, and guide them screen by
screen.
Stay on the line while they do it. Many of our patients are older, and a login link sent now and
used later is often lost.
Login link expires before the patient uses it
PATIENT: "The link expires in 15 minutes." · "Can you text me the link?"
Page 15 of 19

The login link is sent by email only. It can't be sent by text message: Dosable creates a new
link each time, so there's no fixed link you could send another way.
Right after the link is sent, ask the patient to check their email while you're still on the call, in
both the inbox and the spam folder, and click it right away.
If it expired, send a new one and stay on the line while they open it.
Side Effects & Medical Questions
07
You are not clinical staff. You never give medical advice and never interpret a symptom.
Patient reports a side effect or allergy
Follow the side-effect box in §3: 911 first if it's severe and happening now, then cancel in Dosable,
ask them to report it in the Medical Chat, and log it in their words.
Provider asked a question or requested an ID
Follow the Medical Chat playbook. You bring the patient to the chat, where they answer the
provider or send the ID.
If the patient doesn't want to send it through the chat, they can email it to
support@standardmeds.com, from the email on their order.
You never receive the answer or the ID yourself.
"I read that naltrexone is for addiction"
PATIENT: "I'm not addicted to opioids." · "Why did you send me an addiction drug?"
Some NeuroCalmRx patients search the ingredient, find it described as an addiction treatment, and
cancel.
WHAT YOU TELL THEM
"That's a common concern. The addiction treatment uses naltrexone at 50 mg. Your formula
uses low-dose naltrexone, 4.5 mg, less than a tenth of that. At this low dose it works
differently, and providers prescribe it for chronic nerve discomfort. It's not an opioid and it
isn't habit-forming. If you'd like to know more, your provider can answer in the Medical Chat."
Page 16 of 19

Say only this. Don't add claims about what it treats or cures. Any other medical question goes to
the provider in the Medical Chat.
"My own doctor told me not to take it"
Don't argue with the patient's doctor. If they want to stop, cancel right away, no offer. See the box
in §3.
"I don't know the doctor who prescribed this"
PATIENT: "Who is this doctor?" · "I never saw anyone." · "Is this legit?"
WHAT YOU TELL THEM
Standard Meds is a telehealth company. Prescriptions are written by our partner medical
providers, from Beluga Health.
They are real, licensed providers. The provider reviewed the patient's answers before
prescribing.
This is a legal and common way to get treatment. It's faster and more comfortable: the patient
doesn't have to go to a doctor's office.
If they have questions for the provider, send them to the Medical Chat.
"Standard Meds is a telehealth company. Your prescription was written by one of our partner
providers at Beluga Health, after reviewing your answers. They're all real, licensed medical
providers. It works just like a doctor's visit, without you having to go to an office. If you'd like
to ask your provider anything, you can do it in the Medical Chat."
Refunds
08
Refunds are given in specific cases, under our refund policy. Standard Meds decides each
case. Your part is to pass it on.
Any refund or return request
PATIENT: "I want my money back." · "Can I return it?" · "Where is my refund?"
WHAT YOU DO
Don't promise a refund, and don't refuse one. The one exception is a damaged or leaking
package (§5).
Page 17 of 19

Post the order ID in our shared Slack channel (Logicall × Standard Meds), saying the patient
asked for a refund. Order ID only, no name, email or phone. Standard Meds takes it from there.
Tell the patient our team will review the request and get back to them.
"I saw you have a 90-day guarantee"
Don't bring up the 90-day guarantee yourself. Not in a support call, not as a retention
argument.
If the patient mentions it, you can confirm it exists. Post the order ID in our shared Slack
channel, saying the patient is asking to use the guarantee. Standard Meds processes it.
Other Situations
09
The caller isn't the patient
PATIENT: "I'm calling for my husband, he has dementia." · "This is her daughter."
This happens often, especially with upgrade charges on older patients' cards.
Order and health details are health information protected by law. Don't share any order
details with anyone but the patient.
Ask the family member to email support@standardmeds.com.
"Stop contacting me"
1. Mark the patient as do-not-call on your side immediately and end the call politely.
2. Post the order ID in our shared Slack channel, saying the patient asked to stop being contacted.
We remove them from our email and text message flows.
3. The patient can also email support@standardmeds.com.
"I couldn't reach anyone"
Our support line is (302) 291-7264, answered by whoever is live, 9 am – 5 pm Central. Written
requests go to support@standardmeds.com.
"I haven't bought yet, I have questions"
Page 18 of 19

That's a sales call, not support. You can pitch the product they're interested in, using its vertical
playbook from the hub.
Send the quiz link, never a checkout link. The patient has to go through the quiz first.
PRODUCT QUIZ LINK TO SEND
LiftRx standardmeds.com/quiz/liftrx-v3
NeuroCalmRx standardmeds.com/quiz/neuropathy-v2
TriShotRx standardmeds.com/quiz/trishot-v2
ZoliraRx standardmeds.com/quiz/zolirarx-v2
Open Topics
10
Anything still to be defined, in one place.
Nothing is open right now. If you run into a situation this page doesn't cover, post it in our
shared Slack channel (§1), and it will be added here.
